entries.title: Galatians 2:1
segments: After fourteen years. Commentators differ as to whether this period should be counted from Paul's conversion or from his previous visit.  At all events the occasion seems to be, beyond dispute, the council of the apostles and elders recorded in

entries.title: Galatians 2:2
segments: By revelation. Compare

.
 

 
 Laid before them the gospel which I preach. Paul may have thought his teaching might be condemned by the apostles, as it had been by men from Judea (
).  In this private conference, however, with those who were of repute, probably James, Peter and John (
), Paul was upheld.

entries.title: Galatians 2:3
segments: Not even Titus who was with me, etc.  The contention of the Judaizers was that the Gentile Christians must be circumcised to partake of the gospel.  Paul's argument, doubtless in the line of
and
, prevailed.

entries.title: Galatians 2:6
segments: Imparted nothing to me. The revelation to Paul had been so complete and had been received with such faith and intelligence that even the apostles who had been personally in the company of Jesus could add nothing to his understanding of the gospel.

entries.title: Galatians 2:7
segments: When they saw that I had been intrusted. As the Lord said unto Ananias (

), Paul was 'a chosen vessel' to bear His name 'before the Gentiles.'
 

 
 Gospel of the circumcision.  The gospel of those of the circumcision, the Jews; in the words of Peter 'to the elect who are sojourners of the Dispersion' (

entries.title: Galatians 2:9
segments: James and Cephas and John. This James was the brother of the Lord, who had taken the place of James the son of Zebedee, slain by Herod (
).  Cephas was Peter (
).  John was the beloved apostle, the son of Zebedee (

).
 

 
 The right hands of fellowship. A token of agreement in the faith, and of unity of feeling and purpose.

entries.title: Galatians 2:10
segments: Remember the poor. These were evidently the poor among the Jews at Jerusalem.  That the Gentiles, under Paul, did make such contributions is evident from

entries.title: Galatians 2:11
segments:
When Cephas came to Antioch.  This is believed to have been previous to the visit of Paul to Jerusalem recounted in the preceding verses.
 

 
 He stood condemned.   Peter had been taught not to make a distinction between Jews and Gentiles.  See

entries.title: Galatians 2:12
segments: Ate with the Gentiles. The Jews were restricted to certain foods (
).  The Gentiles were not under this law.

entries.title: Galatians 2:13
segments: Even Barnabas was carried away.  Barnabas, although the appointed assistant to Paul in the preaching of the gospel to the Gentiles (
), was a Jew, and a Levite (
).  He was the cousin of Mark the evangelist.

entries.title: Galatians 2:14
segments: Before them all. Paul felt that the unity of the church was imperiled by Peter's movement toward retaining the old line of separation between Jew and Gentile, and he made his remonstrance publicly.  Paul's rebuke of Peter seems to end with
.  The remainder of the chapter is a plea to the dissembling Jews.

entries.title: Galatians 2:18
segments: Those things which I destroyed. After preaching that justification was not by the law, but through faith, Paul argues that he cannot now claim justification through the observance of Jewish customs which were a part of the law.

entries.title: Galatians 2:19
segments: For I through the law died unto the law. The law was 'our tutor' to bring us to Christ (
).  When the law, his tutor, had brought Paul to Christ, he was no longer under the tutor, but had outgrown the necessity for him.

entries.title: Galatians 2:20
segments: Crucified with Christ. See
; also

entries.title: Galatians 2:21
segments: Died for nought. Paul's argument is that Christ died to redeem men from the law and its curse upon the lawbreaker. But if righteousness was still a matter of justification under the law, the death of Christ had been of no avail.
